Definition: Personal data ordered deleted yet still present somewhere in the organization's systems.
Example_From_Challenge: The 'deleted' Northstar customer whose email still triggered 'already registered'.
Why_It_Matters: The entire challenge exists to find and prove the absence of ghost data.

Definition: A formal user request that the organization erase their personal data.
Example_From_Challenge: The requests listed in dataset/deletion_requests.csv, each awaiting a verdict.
Why_It_Matters: Each request is one unit of work the agent must judge and document.

Definition: Any value that points to a person: email, username, account ID, phone number.
Example_From_Challenge: The registered email that refused the customer's re-registration.
Why_It_Matters: Exposure is measured per identifier; every one must be searched everywhere.

Definition: An identifier the person used in the past and may no longer use.
Example_From_Challenge: An old email or previous username left in logs and exports.
Why_It_Matters: Ghost data hides under legacy identifiers a current-only search would miss.

Definition: Any data store beyond the primary account service that mirrors or supplements user data.
Example_From_Challenge: Customer tables inside reporting or CRM databases.
Why_It_Matters: Deletions applied only to the primary service leave ghosts here.

Definition: Files uploaded during support conversations that may embed personal data.
Example_From_Challenge: A screenshot attachment showing the customer's email address.
Why_It_Matters: Often images — the reason local media files must be read.

Definition: An inverted index that makes records searchable and can outlive the source row.
Example_From_Challenge: The customer still findable via search after account deletion.
Why_It_Matters: Indexes preserve exposure even when the database row is gone.

Definition: Snapshot files produced for analysis that freeze data at export time.
Example_From_Challenge: A CSV export containing pre-deletion customer profiles.
Why_It_Matters: Exports are static copies; each must receive its rule-required treatment.

Definition: Timestamped records of system events that may embed personal values.
Example_From_Challenge: An authentication log line containing the deleted email.
Why_It_Matters: Logs are copies too; the rules decide delete, redact, or keep.

Definition: Long-term compressed storage of old records.
Example_From_Challenge: Monthly archives holding past account snapshots.
Why_It_Matters: Archived copies count as exposure unless the rules permit retention.

Definition: Point-in-time copies kept for disaster recovery.
Example_From_Challenge: Nightly backups still containing the deleted profile.
Why_It_Matters: Backups commonly resurrect ghosts on restore; purge or expire them.

Definition: A background process copying data between systems on a schedule.
Example_From_Challenge: The sync job that recreated the deleted customer's information.
Why_It_Matters: The canonical recreation risk: it can silently undo a successful deletion.

Definition: A pipeline that loads external or staged data into a system.
Example_From_Challenge: An import job reloading old user rows from a staging file.
Why_It_Matters: Any import path touching user identifiers can recreate deleted data.

Definition: A procedure that returns a system to a previous state from backups.
Example_From_Challenge: A restore drill that would bring deleted rows back to life.
Why_It_Matters: COMPLETE requires that no restore path can resurrect the data.

Definition: The chance an active process re-creates data that was already deleted.
Example_From_Challenge: A sync job still scheduled while the deletion is being processed.
Why_It_Matters: Deleting copies without killing sources makes remediation futile.

Definition: The AI system that investigates records and issues evidence-backed deletion verdicts.
Example_From_Challenge: The agent this challenge asks you to build.
Why_It_Matters: It must prove erasure, never trust status flags.

Definition: Verdict that deletion is fully done and proven across all four criteria.
Example_From_Challenge: A request whose copies are gone, sources dead, retention intact.
Why_It_Matters: One of the three graded status values in the output.

Definition: Verdict that residual data or live recreation paths remain.
Example_From_Challenge: A request where backups still hold the customer's email.
Why_It_Matters: INCOMPLETE verdicts must come with ordered remediation steps.

Definition: Verdict that the person never requested deletion, so no obligation exists.
Example_From_Challenge: A subject with no matching deletion request on file.
Why_It_Matters: Miscalling this COMPLETE or INCOMPLETE is a grading error.

Definition: The corrective work needed to finish or prove a deletion.
Example_From_Challenge: Killing the sync job, purging backups, redacting old logs.
Why_It_Matters: The agent's actionable output for every INCOMPLETE case.

Definition: Permanently delete the copy entirely.
Example_From_Challenge: Purging the email row from a secondary database.
Why_It_Matters: One of the three treatments deletion_rules.csv may require.

Definition: Mask or strip sensitive fields while keeping the record itself.
Example_From_Challenge: Blanking the email inside a retained invoice.
Why_It_Matters: Enables retention without keeping unauthorized identifiers.

Definition: Transform data so it can no longer be linked to the person.
Example_From_Challenge: Hashing identifiers inside an analytics export.
Why_It_Matters: Turns personal data into non-personal data per the rules.

Definition: Numbered steps sequenced so earlier actions cannot be undone by later effects.
Example_From_Challenge: Disable the sync first, then delete copies, then verify.
Why_It_Matters: Wrong order lets active processes recreate what was just removed.

Definition: The obligation to keep certain records for legal or business reasons.
Example_From_Challenge: Financial records the supplied policy says must be kept.
Why_It_Matters: Retention overrides deletion for protected records.

Definition: A record kept because the policy requires the organization to preserve it.
Example_From_Challenge: The invoice kept, but with the email redacted.
Why_It_Matters: Must contain only permitted identifiers and must stay available.

Definition: An identifier the rules allow to remain inside retained records.
Example_From_Challenge: Internal account ID allowed; email and phone not allowed.
Why_It_Matters: The whitelist that bounds exactly what retention may keep.

Definition: The rule file mapping data types and locations to required treatments.
Example_From_Challenge: Rules specifying purge for backups, redact for logs.
Why_It_Matters: It is the source of truth for every treatment decision.

Definition: The dataset of deletion requests the agent must process and answer.
Example_From_Challenge: dataset/deletion_requests.csv, some rows with expected outputs.
Why_It_Matters: Every row must produce exactly one schema-valid output row.

Definition: A provided reference answer shipped with some of the requests.
Example_From_Challenge: Requests that include known verdicts for self-testing.
Why_It_Matters: Anchors the evaluation workflow before submission.

Definition: The populated result file uploaded for grading.
Example_From_Challenge: One row per request in the exact required schema.
Why_It_Matters: Schema mismatches fail the auto-grader instantly.

Definition: The zipped code/ directory uploaded to the HackerRank platform.
Example_From_Challenge: A zip excluding data/, dataset/, virtualenvs, node_modules.
Why_It_Matters: Dirty archives violate the stated submission rules.

Definition: The AI usage log from the mandated path, uploaded as evidence.
Example_From_Challenge: log.txt recording how AI helped build the solution.
Why_It_Matters: Required upload; must remain unedited.

Definition: A 30-minute camera-on interview probing your understanding of the submission.
Example_From_Challenge: Questions on approach, decisions, and AI usage after submitting.
Why_It_Matters: Shipping code you cannot explain will show immediately.

Definition: Unseen evaluation cases applied once the submission is in.
Example_From_Challenge: Requests withheld until after submission.
Why_It_Matters: Generality, not memorized answers, is what survives them.

Definition: A built-in process that systematically validates the agent's results.
Example_From_Challenge: Comparing predictions to expected outputs and iterating prompts.
Why_It_Matters: A stated mandatory requirement, not optional polish.

Definition: Request-specific answers or test labels written directly into code.
Example_From_Challenge: A dictionary mapping request IDs to verdicts.
Why_It_Matters: Explicitly forbidden; the AI Judge will probe for it.

Definition: A model that reads and reasons over images.
Example_From_Challenge: Extracting the email visible in an attachment screenshot.
Why_It_Matters: Media files mandate a multimodal processing path.

Definition: Large language model used for reasoning over records and rules.
Example_From_Challenge: Summarizing timelines and choosing per-request verdicts.
Why_It_Matters: The reasoning engine behind the audit decisions.

Definition: Prompt design that forces parseable, schema-bound model outputs.
Example_From_Challenge: JSON verdicts with evidence fields attached.
Why_It_Matters: Reliable downstream code needs reliable model output.
